title: bug: importee-guard-bash.test.mjs "Bash stream parser refuses a tool path holding a control character" (added by 96c4ee19, task-414eae5a) compares the parser's witness file and stdout as LF-only, but Windows Python writes text-mode CRLF, so the case fails under Windows node and CI's Windows "Test Bash landing and postflight runner" step has been red since 11-02
description:
Filed by hunt #22 (task-7a3640da), from a dry run of CI's windows-latest leg at fec9a842 on the Windows host.

PROBLEM
- The case at scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs:298-326 runs STREAM_JSON_PARSER with `python`, which is the win32 choice at :12. It makes two assertions:
  - :321 `readFileSync(tools, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean)` deep-equals ['plain.txt'];
  - :323 `run.stdout.includes(\`  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: ${raw}\n\`)`, once for each refused raw path.
- The parser writes the witness file in text mode (`open(harvest_path, 'a', encoding='utf-8')`, moe-agent.sh:11925) and writes stdout in text mode too. On Windows, Python then turns every '\n' into '\r\n', including the '\n' inside the refused raw paths.
- Production is not affected. resolve_attribution reads the file with `line.rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')` (moe-agent.sh:4516), and the WARN lines are display only. This is a test-only defect.
- 96c4ee19's verification ran the file under Linux node only. ubuntu-latest passes; windows-latest's "Test Bash landing and postflight runner" step (ci.yml:289-290) fails.

EVIDENCE (Windows node 24.16.0 and Python 3.14, outside the shared checkout)
- CI emulation of the windows-latest leg at fec9a842: a Windows-git clone at D:\moe-scratch\h22\w with a runner-like environment. The step exited 1 with tests 64, pass 63, fail 1. Log: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-7a3640da/logs/w-15-Test-Bash-landing-and-postflight-runner.log
- First error lines:
  ✖ Bash stream parser refuses a tool path holding a control character, forging no second witness line
    AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected values to be strictly deep-equal:
    + actual - expected
      [
    +   'plain.txt\r'
    -   'plain.txt'
      ]
        at TestContext.<anonymous> (file:///D:/moe-scratch/h22/w/scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs:321:12)
- Bisect, single file under Windows node on a git-archive of scripts and docs:
  - 617c5658 (96c4ee19^): 40/40 pass;
  - 96c4ee19: 41 tests, 1 fail (this case).
  TAPs: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-7a3640da/bisect2/{pre,at}.tap
- Fixing only :321 exposes :323. The real stdout holds `...harvested: ok.txt\r\nforged.txt\r\n`, which does not include `ok.txt\nforged.txt\n`.
- Fix check: with `.split(/\r?\n/)` at :321 and `run.stdout.replaceAll('\r\n', '\n').includes(...)` at :323, the file passes 41/41 under Windows node and 41/41 under Linux node (/mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-7a3640da/fixcheck/).

FIX DIRECTION
- Test-only: turn CRLF into LF before both assertions. Replacing only '\r\n' pairs keeps the lone '\r' in the Write case's raw path, so that check still bites. A one-line comment should say why: Windows Python writes text-mode CRLF.
- Do not change STREAM_JSON_PARSER or moe-agent.sh; their reader already accepts CRLF.
- Leave the ps1 twin alone. scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1, also from 96c4ee19, passed on PowerShell 5.1 and 7 (53/53) in the same run.

FILES: scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs only.
definitionOfDone: Run from a git-archive snapshot of scripts and docs outside the shared checkout, `"/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs` reports at least 41 tests with fail 0.
Under Linux node the same file reports fail 0.

`git diff --stat` for the task names only scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs. The case still asserts that the witness file holds exactly ['plain.txt'] and that each of the 3 refused raw paths has its WARN line.

implementationPlan.description:
Fold CRLF before the two assertions of the one failing test. This is a test-only change. Write it with your Edit tool (global rail: a sed/heredoc write leaves no TOOL witness). The file is scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs, test 'Bash stream parser refuses a tool path holding a control character, forging no second witness line' (:298-326).
(a) Right after `assert.equal(run.status, 0, run.stderr);` (:319), add exactly:
    // Windows Python writes both in text mode (CRLF). Fold only CRLF pairs, so a lone CR in a raw path must still match.
    const lf = text => text.replaceAll('\r\n', '\n');
(b) Line :321 becomes `assert.deepEqual(lf(readFileSync(tools, 'utf8')).split('\n').filter(Boolean), ['plain.txt']);`
(c) Line :323 becomes `assert.ok(lf(run.stdout).includes(`  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: ${raw}\n`), run.stdout);`
The net diff is +4/-2. Keep everything else byte for byte: the `calls` table (the 3 refused raws, i.e. the Edit LF raw, the Write lone-CR raw and the Serena LF raw, plus plain.txt), the expected ['plain.txt'], the expected WARN template, the existing 'not vacuous' comment, `python` at :12, and every other test.
Why fold only CRLF pairs:
- STREAM_JSON_PARSER writes its WARN lines with sys.stdout.write (scripts/moe-agent.sh:11922) and the witness file with open(harvest_path, 'a', encoding='utf-8') (:11925). Both are text mode, so Windows Python turns every LF into CRLF, including the LF inside a refused raw path. A lone CR passes through unchanged.
- Production's reader (:4515-4517, rstrip('\n').rstrip('\r')) already accepts CRLF.
- A lone CR is the forging vector the Write case covers. Never fold a lone CR (no /\r/g, no split(/\r|\n/)), and never normalize the expected side. Either one makes the Write check unmatchable or vacuous.
Do NOT edit scripts/moe-agent.sh, scripts/moe-agent.ps1 or scripts/tests/importee-guard.ps1. The ps1 twin passed 53/53 on PS 5.1 and 7 in hunt #22.
Error handling: no new IO or process is added. A failed parser run still surfaces first through `assert.equal(run.status, 0, run.stderr)`, and `lf` only takes strings the test has already read.
RED at the base is already recorded, so you need not re-run it. At 566778a0, Windows node gave 41 tests / 40 pass / 1 fail at :321 with actual ['plain.txt\r']; Linux node gave 41/41.
This file executes the real parser text cut out of moe-agent.sh: mem:gotcha-wrapper-slice-tests-execute-text.

Verification: run this gate ONCE, from your task worktree, exactly as written. It builds its own git-archive snapshot of scripts and docs under /mnt/d/moe-scratch, copies your edited test file into it, and runs no test inside the checkout (global rail). Gate:
( set -eo pipefail; R=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel); S=$(mktemp -d /mnt/d/moe-scratch/gate-ce263197.XXXXXX); git -C "$R" archive HEAD scripts docs | tar -x -C "$S"; cp "$R/scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs" "$S/scripts/tests/"; cd "$S"; echo "snapshot=$S"; F=scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs; N="/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe"; set +e; "$N" --test "$F" > win.txt 2>&1; w=$?; env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" node --test "$F" > lin.txt 2>&1; l=$?; "$N" --test "$F" scripts/tests/hook-isolation-bash.test.mjs scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs > step.txt 2>&1; s=$?; grep -H -E "^ℹ (tests|pass|fail) " win.txt lin.txt step.txt; awk '/^ℹ tests /{n=$3} END{exit !(n>=41)}' win.txt && awk '/^ℹ tests /{n=$3} END{exit !(n>=41)}' lin.txt; c=$?; echo "exit win=$w lin=$l step=$s count=$c"; [ "$w$l$s$c" = 0000 ] )
Expected result:
- The gate prints `exit win=0 lin=0 step=0 count=0` and exits 0.
- Windows node and Linux node each report tests 41 (at least 41) and fail 0 (DoD 1 and 2).
- The whole CI step (ci.yml:289-290, all three files) under Windows node reports tests 64, fail 0. It was 64 tests / 63 pass / 1 fail at 566778a0.
Submit this output as the verification evidence for complete_task.
DoD 3, run in the worktree: `git diff --stat HEAD && [ "$(git diff --name-only HEAD)" = scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs ]`. It must list only that file (about +4/-2). QA proves the same on the landed commit with `git show --stat --format= <completion>`.
The gate needs a WSL seat because it runs Windows node through /mnt/c. Do not wrap node.exe in env -i: it needs WSL_INTEROP, and it receives only WSLENV vars anyway, so no MOE_* var leaks in. The Linux leg runs under env -i so the seat's MOE_* env cannot leak in. If either path is missing on your seat, call moe.report_blocked instead of substituting another engine.
Error handling: if a leg fails, read win.txt, lin.txt and step.txt in the printed snapshot before changing anything (mem:gotcha-launcher-ps1-rows-from-wsl, mem:gotcha-git-bash-native-env-conversion-and-function-stubs).
Afterwards, remove the snapshot by its literal printed path (rm -rf /mnt/d/moe-scratch/gate-ce263197.<suffix>).

Adversarial self-review of your diff (final step). Prove the fold kept the case's teeth with three mutants.
1. Copy the step-2 snapshot three times (cp -r <snapshot> <snapshot>-<mode>; these are scratch copies outside the checkout).
2. Apply one mutant per copy: node /mnt/d/moe-scratch/arch-ce263197/logs/patch.cjs <mut|mutcr|mutwarn> <copy>. Each mode edits only that copy's scripts/moe-agent.sh, exactly once. If that file is gone, make the same edits by hand in the copy:
   - mut: `        return None if re.search(r'[\x00-\x1f]', rest) else rest` becomes `        return rest`, and `    if not p or re.search(r'[\x00-\x1f]', p) or any(` becomes `    if not p or any(`.
   - mutcr: in the same two lines, `re.search(r'[\x00-\x1f]', X)` becomes `'\n' in X`.
   - mutwarn: `            w('  [WARN] tool write outside the repo not harvested: %s\n' % raw)` becomes `            pass`.
3. In each copy, run `"/mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe" --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs` and `env -i HOME="$HOME" PATH="$PATH" node --test scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs`.
Every run must exit 1 with only this case failing:
- mut (no control-character refusal) fails on a forged 'ok.txt' witness line;
- mutcr (LF-only refusal) fails on 'a.txt\rforged.txt';
- mutwarn (WARN print dropped) fails at the WARN assertion.
The architect's runs of these mutants all went red on both engines (TAPs in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/arch-ce263197/logs).
Then answer each of these:
- Can lf ever fold a CR that is not followed by LF? It must not.
- Are the expected strings and the calls table unchanged?
- Is the diff exactly the one file?
- Can two runs collide? No: each test makes its own mkdtemp scratch.
If this review changes the file, re-run the step-2 gate and submit that fresh output to complete_task.
Remove the mutant copies by literal path.

It folds CRLF pairs to LF in the witness-file text and in the parser's stdout before its existing assertions, so text-mode CRLF from Windows Python no longer fails it. It still asserts that the witness file holds exactly ['plain.txt'] and that each of the 3 refused raw paths gets its WARN line. Linux behavior is unchanged, and so is production code.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
The test executes the real STREAM_JSON_PARSER text cut out of scripts/moe-agent.sh, so a parser regression shows up here. Windows Python's text mode writes each LF as CRLF and leaves a lone CR alone; Node reads both as-is. From WSL, /mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe gets only WSLENV vars and resolves the Windows `python` (3.14 on this host).

epic-be924fb8 has no finalTaskId, so this row's isEpicFinal:true comes from the max-order fallback in a rolling bug bucket. The gate is therefore scoped to the one CI step this row repairs, not to a whole-epic sweep.
planningNotes.risks:
(1) Weakening the case: folding a lone CR, or normalizing the expected side, makes the lone-CR Write check vacuous. The mutcr mutant catches this.
(2) Running node --test in the shared checkout or the worktree instead of the snapshot. The gate builds its own snapshot, so run it as written.
(3) Shell-writing the test file (sed/heredoc) leaves no TOOL witness. Use the Edit tool.
(4) env -i on node.exe drops WSL_INTEROP, which is why the gate uses env -i only on the Linux leg.
(5) The gate needs /mnt/d/moe-scratch and /mnt/c/Program Files/nodejs/node.exe, i.e. a WSL seat. Without them, block; never substitute another engine, because the DoD names Windows node.
(6) Leave the ps1 twin (importee-guard.ps1) and both launchers alone.
